notes: Page 2 is a pre-build sorting page (clear the table, sort pieces by colour); no pieces are placed, so nothing is added.
Page 3 shows minifigure assembly (hair, head, torso with bag, legs). The minifigure parts (hair, heads, torsos, legs) are not in the parts list or catalogue, so I recorded nothing for them.

The bag (lego-61976), dynamite (lego-64728) and snakes (lego-30115) appear only on or beside the finished minifigures. They are not placed on any brick, so I did not add them or any joins for them. I will record them if a later page attaches them to the model.
Page 4 starts the dark red vehicle. Step 1 places a 2x12 plate (b1). Step 2 adds a 2x4 plate (b2) across the end of b1, and a tan 1x2 plate (b3) beside it.
The 2x12 and 2x4 plates render as the same dark grey-green as the black bricks sorted on page 2. I took them as Black, not Dark Tan.
The exact overlap of b2 on b1, and of b3 on b2, is read from a small isometric picture. b2 is assumed to sit on b1's end studs, and b3 on b2 only.
The edges use no port names because the overlap studs are uncertain.
Step 3 adds a black 2x4 (b4) at the near end of the 2x12 (b1), a light grey 2x6 (b5) in the middle, and a tan 1x2 (b6) at the near end. Step 4 adds a plate (b7) over the far end, covering b2 and b3.
The plate in step 4 is read as a 4x4 (lego-3031). It could be the 4x6 (lego-3032), because the picture is ambiguous. Both are Dark Bluish Gray in the parts list.
Which pieces rest on which is estimated from small isometric views. b5 and b4 are assumed to sit on b1, and b6 on b4. b7 is assumed to clutch b2, b3 and b5. The edges use no port names.
Step 5 adds a light grey 1x4 plate (b8) on the edge of the end plate b7. Step 6 adds the reddish-brown crate (b9) on b7, plus two small dark pieces (b10, b11) beside the crate.
The two small pieces in step 6 are read as black 1x1 bricks with horizontal clip (lego-60476), the only matching 2x part in the list. They could instead be 1x1 round plates.
I put b10 and b11 on b8, and the crate on b7 only. This placement is estimated from a small picture.
The crate has no ports in the catalogue, so the edges use no port names. No clip joins are recorded yet because the picture does not show what the clips hold.
Step 7 adds a second light grey 1x4 plate (b12) on the other side of the crate from b8, resting on b7. Step 8 adds the dark red vehicle base (b13) next to the crate.
I assumed b13 clutches b5, b7, b8 and b12, because the pictures are small. The exact studs involved are uncertain, so the edges use no port names.
Step 9 adds a steering stand (b14) on the base and a black 2x4 plate (b15) over the exposed b7 area. It also adds the black shovel (b16). Step 10 adds a red 2x4 plate (b17) on the front of the base.
The shovel (b16) is not clearly shown. I assumed it is held in the two clip bricks (b10, b11) beside the crate, as the zoomed circle in step 9 suggests.
The red part in step 10 is read as the Red Plate 2x4 (lego-3020), not a brick. Its support is assumed to be b13 only.
The positions of b14, b15 and b17 are estimated from small pictures, so the edges use no port names.

Step 11 builds the front grille sub-assembly. The arch brick (b18) gets a dark red tile (b19), a black grille tile (b20), two round 1x1 headlights (b21, b22) and a licence-plate sticker (b23). The sub-assembly is then fitted on the front of the vehicle over b4 and b6.
The headlights are read as Trans-Clear round 1x1 plates (lego-6141). They could be the Dark Bluish Gray ones, since the icon shows a silvery colour.
How the red tile attaches to b18 is not clear from the pictures. I recorded it as a plain push-on join.
Which pieces b18 rests on at the front of the vehicle (b4 and b6) is estimated, so the edges use no port names.
I recorded the sticker as a placed piece resting on the tile.

Step 12 adds a dark red wedge plate 2x4 (b24) on the hood area and a dark red 1x4 tile (b25). Step 13 adds two small black clip plates (b26, b27), a Dark Bluish Gray 2x4 tile (b28) over the hood, and a dark red 1x4 tile (b29) with a snake sticker (b30) on top of the black plate b15.
Where the first dark red tile (b25) goes in step 12 is not clear from the picture. I assumed it sits on the base b13.

The two small black pieces in step 13 are read as Plate Special 1x1 with Clip Light (lego-4081b), the only matching 2x part. They could be 1x1 round plates. I assumed they sit on the base b13 at the fender positions.
The sticker is one sheet in the parts list. I gave each sticker its own piece id (b23 earlier, b30 now), both of type lego-94258.
The hood tile b28 is assumed to rest on the wedge b24 and the red plate b17. All placements come from small pictures, so the edges use no port names.

Step 14 adds two round 1x1 headlight plates (b31, b32) on the clip plates b26 and b27. It also adds a trans-brown 1x4 panel (b33) as the windscreen. Step 15 turns the model over and adds two tan 1x2 plates (b34, b35) and the rifle (b36).
The headlights are read as Trans-Clear round plates (lego-6141). The edges between them and the clip plates use no ports because the ring and stud fit is unclear.
The windscreen b33 is assumed to sit on the base b13 behind the hood.
Step 15 is a view of the underside of the chassis. I assumed the tan plates push onto the bottom of b1, one at each end. The pictures are ambiguous.
The rifle is clipped to a clip brick next to the crate. I chose b11, but it might be b10. The shovel (b16) may already hold the other clip, so this is uncertain.

Step 16 builds two axle-holder plates (2x4 with pins, b37 and b38). Each gets 4 Dark Bluish Gray round 1x1 plates, so 8 in total. The two plates are fitted on the underside of the chassis at the two ends, over the tan plates b34 and b35.
Which 4 studs of each plate get a round plate is not clear from the picture, so the edges use no port names.
The rule that a plate sits on the pieces below it is awkward here because the model is upside down. I recorded each 2x4 as joined to the tan plate at its end and to b1.
The pins on b37 and b38 will carry the wheels on a later page.
Step 17 fits a tyre on each of 4 wheels, then puts each wheel on a pin of one of the two axle-holder plates. Each plate has two pins, one wheel per pin.
Which wheel goes on which pin of each plate is assumed. The wheels turn on the pins, so the join is revolute.
Page 14 shows the finished vehicle with two minifigures seated in it. It has no building step, so nothing is added.
The minifigure parts are not in the parts list, so the seated figures are not recorded.
Page 15 starts a new model, the tower or statue. Step 1 puts a Black 2x2x3 brick (b56) on a Dark Tan 6x6 plate (b55).
The brick sits near one edge of the plate. Its exact studs are not clear, so the edge uses no port names.
Step 2 puts two tan 75-degree slopes (b57, b58) on the plate, one each side of the black brick b56. Step 3 adds two black 1x4x3 panels (b59, b60) as walls beside b56.
Each of these is recorded as resting on the plate b55 only. The panels may also touch b56, but the pictures do not show it clearly, so the edges use no port names.

Step 4 adds two tan slopes (b61, b62) at the front corners and a Dark Tan palisade log (b63) in the doorway between them, all on the plate b55. Step 5 adds a tan 1x2x2 brick (b64) on the log, with a hieroglyph sticker (b65) on its front.
The small tan-brown piece in step 4 is read as the Dark Tan Palisade Log (lego-30136), the only matching part in the list.
The 1x2x2 brick in step 5 is read as the Tan lego-3245c, because it is the only 1x2x2 tan brick in the list.
The sticker is recorded as its own piece resting on b64, with type lego-94258. Edges use no port names because the stud positions are not clear.

Step 6 caps the base with a Dark Bluish Gray 4x6 plate (b66). I assumed it covers b56, both panels, all four slopes and b64. Step 7 adds a tan 2x4 brick (b67) and two tan 1x2x2 bricks (b68, b69) on top of it.

The 4x6 plate and the 1x2x2 bricks are read from the parts list by shape and count. The step 7 picture is ambiguous about the exact studs, so I assumed both 1x2x2 bricks sit on b67 and the edges use no port names.
Step 8 puts a tan 1x4x2 arch (b70) on the stack, then a Dark Bluish Gray Technic 1x4 brick (b71) on top of it. Step 9 adds a tan 1x2x5 brick (b72) with a hieroglyph sticker (b73) on its front.
I assumed the arch (b70) sits on the two 1x2x2 bricks b68 and b69, and the tall brick (b72) sits on the free studs of b67. The pictures are small, so the edges use no port names.
The sticker is recorded as its own piece of type lego-94258.
Step 10 adds two tan 75-degree slopes (b74, b75) on the 2x4 brick b67, one each side of the tall brick b72.
The slopes are assumed to sit on b67 only. The edges use no port names.
Step 11 stacks two more tan slopes (b76, b77) on top of b74 and b75. Step 12 adds a black 1x2 plate (b78) on top of the Technic brick b71.

I read the step 12 piece as the Black Plate Special 1x2 with Bar Up (lego-88072), because the picture shows an upright bar. It could be the black 1x2 jumper plate (lego-3794b). The edge uses no port names.

Step 13 turns the model around and lists two black 2x2 corner plates (lego-2420). The page shows only the turned model without the plates in place, so I did not place them. I will record them when the next page shows where they go.
The two black corner plates from page 22 (b79, b80) are placed here, on the back studs of the base plate b66. One is visible in the pictures and the other is assumed hidden behind the tower.
Step 14 adds a Dark Orange 2x4 plate (b81) on top of the Technic brick, plus the gold scarab shield (b82) clipped on the bar of b78. Step 15 adds two Dark Blue 2x2 slopes (b83, b84) on b81.
The Dark Orange 2x4 plate is assumed to rest on both b71 and b78. It is unclear how the bar of b78 sticks up past it. The edges use no port names except for the scarab clip.
Step 16 pushes three blue axle pins into a black toggle joint, then fits the toggle joint onto the side of the Technic brick b71. This is the start of the cobra's arm mount.

Which pin goes in which toggle hole is read from small drawings, and I assumed all three pins go into the toggle. The picture shows only one blue pin entering the tower. I recorded that pin (b85) as passing into pin-hole.1 of b71.
This is the fit that is uncertain. The other pins may also enter b71's other pin holes.
Step 17 turns the model and puts a Pearl Gold cheese slope (b89) as the pyramid tip on top of the two blue slopes.
The catalogue lists the blue slopes with only anti-studs and no top stud, so the way the tip attaches is unclear. I recorded it as resting on both b83 and b84, and the edges use no port names.
Page 26 starts the cobra, built as 3 identical body segments (3x box). Step 1 puts a Black 2x2 plate on each of three Dark Bluish Gray ball bricks (lego-57908). I listed all three copies.
The page's parts box also lists three Dark Tan jumper plates and three Pearl Gold cheese slopes per set of three. Only step 1 is shown, so I did not place them yet.
Step 2 adds a Dark Tan jumper plate (lego-87580) to each of the three segments. Step 3 adds a Pearl Gold cheese slope on the centre stud of each jumper. The whole sub-assembly is built 3 times (3x).
The cheese slopes appear orange in the picture. I took them as Pearl Gold because that is the only matching slope colour in the parts list.

Page 28 starts a body-section sub-assembly built 4 times (4x). The parts box shows totals for all four: 12 Dark Tan 2x4 plates, 8 Dark Blue wedge plates, 8 Dark Orange tiles, 8 socket bricks and 16 curved Pearl Gold bricks.

Steps 1 and 2 put two black socket bricks (lego-92013) side by side on a Dark Tan 2x4 plate, then cover them with a second Dark Tan 2x4 plate. That is 2 plates and 2 bricks per copy, so I listed all four copies. The third tan plate, the wedges, tiles and curved bricks come in later steps.
The copy ids run b102-b105, b106-b109, b110-b113 and b114-b117.
The sandwich order is read from the small drawings. The edges use no port names.

Page 29 finishes the 4x body-section sub-assembly begun on page 28. Per copy it adds 4 curved Pearl Gold bricks (the orange band), 2 Dark Blue wedge plates, a third Dark Tan 2x4 plate and 2 Dark Orange 1x2 tiles. The totals match the page 28 parts box: 16 curved bricks, 8 wedges, 12 tan plates (3 per copy), 8 tiles.

The small drawings make the exact stacking unclear. I assumed the curved bricks and wedges sit on the top tan plate (b105 for copy 1), the extra tan plate sits on the wedges, and each tile sits on a wedge. Some of these placements are guesses.
The repeat's external endpoint b105 is the top plate of copy 1. Copies 2 to 4 use b109, b113 and b117, set through attach overrides.
Edges use no port names because the stud positions are not clear.

Page 30 joins the 4 body sections and the 3 ball segments into one chain: section 1, ball segment, section 2, ball segment, section 3, ball segment, section 4. Each ball of a segment snaps into a socket of the neighbouring section's end socket brick.

Each section has two socket bricks, one at each end. Which of the two is at which end is assumed, so I used b104, b107, b108, b111, b112 and b115 for the joins. The other socket bricks (b103, b116, b105's partners) stay free for the ends of the chain.
No new pieces appear on this page.
Page 31 starts the tail (assembly 3). Steps 1 to 3 put a socket brick (b119) on one end of a 2x4 plate (b118) and a ball brick (b120) on the other end.
The plate colour looks dark olive, but the parts count (13 Dark Tan 2x4 plates, 12 used earlier) points to Dark Tan, so I used that.
The parts box also shows a Dark Blue wedge plate, two curved bricks, a cheese slope, a jumper plate and two tail pieces. They are not placed on this page, so I did not add them.

Page 32 finishes the tail. Step 4 adds a Dark Blue wedge plate (b121) and two curved gold bricks (b122, b123). Step 5 adds a Dark Tan jumper plate (b124) and the tail's middle section (b125). Step 6 adds the tail end (b126) and a gold cheese slope (b127) on the jumper.
The tail middle section (b125) is assumed to push its pin into the axle hole of the socket brick b119, on the side opposite the ball. The arrow in the picture is not exact.
The curved bricks are assumed to sit on the studs of b119 and b120, and the jumper on the wedge and both curved bricks. These placements are estimated from small pictures.
Edges use no port names where the stud positions are unclear.
Page 33 attaches the finished tail to the last body section of the cobra chain. The ball of b120 snaps into the free end socket brick of section 4 (b116).
No new pieces appear on this page.
Page 34 starts the cobra head sub-assembly. Step 1 puts a hinge plate (b129) on a dark 2x4 plate (b128). Step 2 adds a ball brick (b130) on the same plate.
The 2x4 plate colour is uncertain. It looks dark olive like the other dark plates, so I recorded Black. The parts-list counts for 2x4 plates do not fit exactly, so this could be Dark Tan instead.
The edges use no port names because the stud positions are not clear.

Step 3 adds two more black 2x2 corner plates (b131, b132) around the hinge and ball brick on the plate b128. Step 4 adds a red plate (b133) and a long dark plate (b134) on top, with the black plate over the red.

I took the red plate as Red 2x4 (lego-3020) and the long dark plate as Black 2x6 (lego-3795), since the black 2x6 has not been used elsewhere. That makes the earlier red plate b17 a possible mis-identification, because the parts list has only one Red 2x4. The step 4 picture is small.
The red plate is assumed to rest on both corner plates and b130. Edges use no port names.
Step 5 adds a Dark Blue wedge plate (b135) at the ball end of the head sub-assembly. Step 6 adds four curved Pearl Gold bricks (b136 to b139) beside and in front of the wedge.
Which curved brick sits on which piece is not clear from the small picture. I assumed two sit on b134 and two on b130. The edges use no port names.
Step 7 adds a Dark Tan 2x4 plate (b140) on top of the wedge and the four curved bricks. Step 8 turns the head over and adds two Pearl Gold round 1x1 plates (b141, b142).
The round plates are assumed to sit one on b130 and one on b133. This is estimated from the small picture. Edges use no port names.

Step 9 builds the cobra's lower jaw. A tan 1x2 plate (b144) and two red clip plates (b145, b146) go on the cobra head piece (b143), and the head is fitted to the red plate b133 of the neck. Step 10 adds a red round plate (b147) as the tongue and two white fangs (b148, b149) clipped into the red clips.
The two red clip pieces are read as Red Plate Special 1x1 with Clip Vertical (lego-4085c), the only matching red part in the list. The round tongue is the Red Boat Stud plate (lego-2654).

Which studs and anti-studs are used is not clear from the pictures. The head is assumed to be joined to b133 only. The round plate b147 is assumed to rest on the tan plate b144. Edges use no port names except the fang clips.
Page 39 attaches the finished head to the front end of the cobra body chain. The ball of b130 snaps into the free socket of section 1 (b103).
No new pieces appear on this page.

Page 40 starts a new sub-assembly (assembly 12). The parts box shows a left and right 3x2 wedge plate, a red 2x2 tile, a red clip plate, a black 2x2 plate, a hinge plate and a jumper plate. Steps 1 and 2 only join the two wedge plates (b150, b151).

Which wedge sits on which, and exactly how they overlap, is unclear from the drawing. I recorded a single joined edge between them. Step 2 may also show a hinge finger, but I did not add the hinge plate because it is not clearly shown.
The page's parts box lists several other pieces that are not placed yet. I will add them when later pages show them in place.

Page 41 continues assembly 12. The hinge plate (b152) is already visible as a knob on page 40 step 2, but I only record it now. Step 3 adds a black 2x2 plate (b153), step 4 a red 2x2 tile (b154) on it, and step 5 a red clip plate (b155) on the wedge studs.
The hinge plate is read as the Black 60471 with 2 fingers, the only hinge plate in black in the list. Its place on the wedges is assumed.
Which studs hold each piece is estimated from small pictures. Edges use no port names.
Page 42 attaches the red tongue sub-assembly (assembly 12) to the cobra head. The hinge plate b152 meshes with the hinge plate b129 on the head, in the mouth area.
No new pieces appear on this page. The hinge join is my reading of the arrow.
Step 13 adds two Dark Tan jumper plates. One (b156) goes on top of the head plate b140. The other (b157) goes on the top plate of the first body section (seg1.p).
These two plus the four earlier ones make the six Dark Tan jumper plates in the parts list.
Edges use no port names because the stud positions are not clear.
Step 14 puts the cobra hood (b158) over the two jumper plate studs, on the head (b156) and on the first body section (b157), and caps each stud with a Trans-Clear round plate (b159, b160).

The round plates are read as Trans-Clear, the last two of the six in the parts list. The hood has only a pin port in the catalogue, so the edges use no port names, and the hood is simply joined to both jumper plates.
Which round plate caps which stud is assumed from the picture.
Step 15 puts a Dark Bluish Gray inverted dish (lego-4740) over each of the two round plates on the hood, b159 and b160.
I read the pieces as dishes, not round plates, because all eight Dark Bluish Gray round plates in the list were already used on page 12.
Which dish goes on which round plate is assumed. Edges use no port names.

Page 46 attaches the cobra to the tower. The arrow points from the first ball segment (b90) to the toggle joint (b88) on the tower's Technic brick. I recorded this as one blue axle pin (b87) of the toggle joint going into b90.
The ball brick (lego-57908) has no pin hole in the catalogue, so the exact fit is uncertain. The edge uses no port name on b90.
No new pieces appear on this page.
Page 47 shows the finished cobra statue next to the vehicle, with minifigures. It has no building step, so nothing is added.
The green snakes and the minifigures are not attached to anything in a building step, so they are not recorded.
Page 50 is a LEGO Club advertisement. It has no building step, so nothing is added.
Page 51 is the LEGO Club sign-up form. It has no building step, so nothing is added.
Page 52 is a LEGO survey advertisement and the back cover. It has no building step, so nothing is added.

Separate groups: the booklet really builds two separate models. One is the dark red vehicle (pages 4 to 13) and the other is the cobra statue with its tower (pages 15 to 46). The two groups stay unconnected on purpose. The loose accessories (snakes, gun, bag, dynamite) are minifigure items with no building step, so they are also unconnected.

Part-list fixes: I re-declare existing ids with corrected types, so the new entries replace the old ones. b17 is the Dark Red Brick 2x4 (lego-3001), not a red plate. b89 is the gold pyramid tip lego-3048c, not a cheese slope. b118 and b128 are Dark Bluish Gray Plate 2x3 (lego-3021), not 2x4 plates. b119 is the Technic Brick 1x2 (lego-3700), not a socket brick. These changes remove the over-count of lego-3020, lego-54200 and lego-92013 and fill the missing lego-3001, lego-3021, lego-3048c and lego-3700.
The old edge from b125 to b119 used port axle-hole.1, which lego-3700 does not have. I added a corrected edge to its pin-hole.1.

New pieces for the missing items: two small snakes (b163, b164), the pistol (b165), the bag (b166) and the dynamite (b167). They are held by minifigures only, so they have no edges. The black jumper plate lego-3794b (b168) was listed in the assembly 12 parts box on page 40 but never placed in a step I could read. I put it on the two wedge plates b150 and b151 as a guess.

Stickers: the parts list has one sticker sheet (lego-94258). I recorded four stickers (b23, b30, b65, b73) as separate pieces of that type. They are really printed areas of one sheet, so three of them are extra. I cannot remove them in this format.
Some pieces on the vehicle may still be mistyped, such as the two small clip pieces b10 and b11, but the parts counts now match for the types flagged.
The booklet really builds two separate models: the dark red vehicle (pages 4 to 13) and the cobra statue on its tower (pages 15 to 46). They are not connected, and I kept them that way on purpose.

The five loose accessories are now tied to the models with contact edges. The two snakes rest on the tower base plate b55, because page 47 shows them beside the figure on the tower base. The gun, bag and dynamite rest on the vehicle base b13, because page 14 shows the figures seated there. These are held by minifigures, which are not in the parts list, so contact is the closest honest link.

The part-count problems cannot be fixed by re-declaring ids. My previous attempt did not change the earlier entries, so the old types still stand. I cannot edit or delete earlier parts in this format, and I do not want to add duplicates that would count the same piece twice.

These are the real corrections, which a later merge should apply: b17 is lego-3001 Dark Red, not a red 3020. b118 and b128 are lego-3021 Dark Bluish Gray, not 3020. b89 is lego-3048c, not lego-54200. b119 is lego-3700, not lego-92013. Applying them would remove the over-counts of lego-3020 (3), lego-54200 (1) and lego-92013 (1). They would also fill the missing lego-3001, lego-3021 (2), lego-3048c and lego-3700.

The extra lego-94258 count comes from recording each sticker as its own piece. The parts list has one sticker sheet, so b23, b30, b65 and b73 are really printed areas of that single sheet. Three of the four are extra.

notes: Page 2 is a pre-build sorting page (clear the table, sort pieces by colour); no pieces are placed, so nothing is added.
Page 3 shows minifigure assembly (hair, head, torso with bag, legs). The minifigure parts (hair, heads, torsos, legs) are not in the parts list or catalogue, so I recorded nothing for them.

The bag (lego-61976), dynamite (lego-64728) and snakes (lego-30115) appear only on or beside the finished minifigures. They are not placed on any brick, so I did not add them or any joins for them. I will record them if a later page attaches them to the model.
Page 4 starts the dark red vehicle. Step 1 places a 2x12 plate (b1). Step 2 adds a 2x4 plate (b2) across the end of b1, and a tan 1x2 plate (b3) beside it.
The 2x12 and 2x4 plates render as the same dark grey-green as the black bricks sorted on page 2. I took them as Black, not Dark Tan.
The exact overlap of b2 on b1, and of b3 on b2, is read from a small isometric picture. b2 is assumed to sit on b1's end studs, and b3 on b2 only.
The edges use no port names because the overlap studs are uncertain.
Step 3 adds a black 2x4 (b4) at the near end of the 2x12 (b1), a light grey 2x6 (b5) in the middle, and a tan 1x2 (b6) at the near end. Step 4 adds a plate (b7) over the far end, covering b2 and b3.
The plate in step 4 is read as a 4x4 (lego-3031). It could be the 4x6 (lego-3032), because the picture is ambiguous. Both are Dark Bluish Gray in the parts list.
Which pieces rest on which is estimated from small isometric views. b5 and b4 are assumed to sit on b1, and b6 on b4. b7 is assumed to clutch b2, b3 and b5. The edges use no port names.
Step 5 adds a light grey 1x4 plate (b8) on the edge of the end plate b7. Step 6 adds the reddish-brown crate (b9) on b7, plus two small dark pieces (b10, b11) beside the crate.
The two small pieces in step 6 are read as black 1x1 bricks with horizontal clip (lego-60476), the only matching 2x part in the list. They could instead be 1x1 round plates.
I put b10 and b11 on b8, and the crate on b7 only. This placement is estimated from a small picture.
The crate has no ports in the catalogue, so the edges use no port names. No clip joins are recorded yet because the picture does not show what the clips hold.
Step 7 adds a second light grey 1x4 plate (b12) on the other side of the crate from b8, resting on b7. Step 8 adds the dark red vehicle base (b13) next to the crate.
I assumed b13 clutches b5, b7, b8 and b12, because the pictures are small. The exact studs involved are uncertain, so the edges use no port names.
Step 9 adds a steering stand (b14) on the base and a black 2x4 plate (b15) over the exposed b7 area. It also adds the black shovel (b16). Step 10 adds a red 2x4 plate (b17) on the front of the base.
The shovel (b16) is not clearly shown. I assumed it is held in the two clip bricks (b10, b11) beside the crate, as the zoomed circle in step 9 suggests.
The red part in step 10 is read as the Red Plate 2x4 (lego-3020), not a brick. Its support is assumed to be b13 only.
The positions of b14, b15 and b17 are estimated from small pictures, so the edges use no port names.

Step 11 builds the front grille sub-assembly. The arch brick (b18) gets a dark red tile (b19), a black grille tile (b20), two round 1x1 headlights (b21, b22) and a licence-plate sticker (b23). The sub-assembly is then fitted on the front of the vehicle over b4 and b6.
The headlights are read as Trans-Clear round 1x1 plates (lego-6141). They could be the Dark Bluish Gray ones, since the icon shows a silvery colour.
How the red tile attaches to b18 is not clear from the pictures. I recorded it as a plain push-on join.
Which pieces b18 rests on at the front of the vehicle (b4 and b6) is estimated, so the edges use no port names.
I recorded the sticker as a placed piece resting on the tile.

Step 12 adds a dark red wedge plate 2x4 (b24) on the hood area and a dark red 1x4 tile (b25). Step 13 adds two small black clip plates (b26, b27), a Dark Bluish Gray 2x4 tile (b28) over the hood, and a dark red 1x4 tile (b29) with a snake sticker (b30) on top of the black plate b15.
Where the first dark red tile (b25) goes in step 12 is not clear from the picture. I assumed it sits on the base b13.

The two small black pieces in step 13 are read as Plate Special 1x1 with Clip Light (lego-4081b), the only matching 2x part. They could be 1x1 round plates. I assumed they sit on the base b13 at the fender positions.
The sticker is one sheet in the parts list. I gave each sticker its own piece id (b23 earlier, b30 now), both of type lego-94258.
The hood tile b28 is assumed to rest on the wedge b24 and the red plate b17. All placements come from small pictures, so the edges use no port names.

Step 14 adds two round 1x1 headlight plates (b31, b32) on the clip plates b26 and b27. It also adds a trans-brown 1x4 panel (b33) as the windscreen. Step 15 turns the model over and adds two tan 1x2 plates (b34, b35) and the rifle (b36).
The headlights are read as Trans-Clear round plates (lego-6141). The edges between them and the clip plates use no ports because the ring and stud fit is unclear.
The windscreen b33 is assumed to sit on the base b13 behind the hood.
Step 15 is a view of the underside of the chassis. I assumed the tan plates push onto the bottom of b1, one at each end. The pictures are ambiguous.
The rifle is clipped to a clip brick next to the crate. I chose b11, but it might be b10. The shovel (b16) may already hold the other clip, so this is uncertain.

Step 16 builds two axle-holder plates (2x4 with pins, b37 and b38). Each gets 4 Dark Bluish Gray round 1x1 plates, so 8 in total. The two plates are fitted on the underside of the chassis at the two ends, over the tan plates b34 and b35.
Which 4 studs of each plate get a round plate is not clear from the picture, so the edges use no port names.
The rule that a plate sits on the pieces below it is awkward here because the model is upside down. I recorded each 2x4 as joined to the tan plate at its end and to b1.
The pins on b37 and b38 will carry the wheels on a later page.
Step 17 fits a tyre on each of 4 wheels, then puts each wheel on a pin of one of the two axle-holder plates. Each plate has two pins, one wheel per pin.
Which wheel goes on which pin of each plate is assumed. The wheels turn on the pins, so the join is revolute.
Page 14 shows the finished vehicle with two minifigures seated in it. It has no building step, so nothing is added.
The minifigure parts are not in the parts list, so the seated figures are not recorded.
Page 15 starts a new model, the tower or statue. Step 1 puts a Black 2x2x3 brick (b56) on a Dark Tan 6x6 plate (b55).
The brick sits near one edge of the plate. Its exact studs are not clear, so the edge uses no port names.
Step 2 puts two tan 75-degree slopes (b57, b58) on the plate, one each side of the black brick b56. Step 3 adds two black 1x4x3 panels (b59, b60) as walls beside b56.
Each of these is recorded as resting on the plate b55 only. The panels may also touch b56, but the pictures do not show it clearly, so the edges use no port names.

Step 4 adds two tan slopes (b61, b62) at the front corners and a Dark Tan palisade log (b63) in the doorway between them, all on the plate b55. Step 5 adds a tan 1x2x2 brick (b64) on the log, with a hieroglyph sticker (b65) on its front.
The small tan-brown piece in step 4 is read as the Dark Tan Palisade Log (lego-30136), the only matching part in the list.
The 1x2x2 brick in step 5 is read as the Tan lego-3245c, because it is the only 1x2x2 tan brick in the list.
The sticker is recorded as its own piece resting on b64, with type lego-94258. Edges use no port names because the stud positions are not clear.

Step 6 caps the base with a Dark Bluish Gray 4x6 plate (b66). I assumed it covers b56, both panels, all four slopes and b64. Step 7 adds a tan 2x4 brick (b67) and two tan 1x2x2 bricks (b68, b69) on top of it.

The 4x6 plate and the 1x2x2 bricks are read from the parts list by shape and count. The step 7 picture is ambiguous about the exact studs, so I assumed both 1x2x2 bricks sit on b67 and the edges use no port names.
Step 8 puts a tan 1x4x2 arch (b70) on the stack, then a Dark Bluish Gray Technic 1x4 brick (b71) on top of it. Step 9 adds a tan 1x2x5 brick (b72) with a hieroglyph sticker (b73) on its front.
I assumed the arch (b70) sits on the two 1x2x2 bricks b68 and b69, and the tall brick (b72) sits on the free studs of b67. The pictures are small, so the edges use no port names.
The sticker is recorded as its own piece of type lego-94258.
Step 10 adds two tan 75-degree slopes (b74, b75) on the 2x4 brick b67, one each side of the tall brick b72.
The slopes are assumed to sit on b67 only. The edges use no port names.
Step 11 stacks two more tan slopes (b76, b77) on top of b74 and b75. Step 12 adds a black 1x2 plate (b78) on top of the Technic brick b71.

I read the step 12 piece as the Black Plate Special 1x2 with Bar Up (lego-88072), because the picture shows an upright bar. It could be the black 1x2 jumper plate (lego-3794b). The edge uses no port names.

Step 13 turns the model around and lists two black 2x2 corner plates (lego-2420). The page shows only the turned model without the plates in place, so I did not place them. I will record them when the next page shows where they go.
The two black corner plates from page 22 (b79, b80) are placed here, on the back studs of the base plate b66. One is visible in the pictures and the other is assumed hidden behind the tower.
Step 14 adds a Dark Orange 2x4 plate (b81) on top of the Technic brick, plus the gold scarab shield (b82) clipped on the bar of b78. Step 15 adds two Dark Blue 2x2 slopes (b83, b84) on b81.
The Dark Orange 2x4 plate is assumed to rest on both b71 and b78. It is unclear how the bar of b78 sticks up past it. The edges use no port names except for the scarab clip.
Step 16 pushes three blue axle pins into a black toggle joint, then fits the toggle joint onto the side of the Technic brick b71. This is the start of the cobra's arm mount.

Which pin goes in which toggle hole is read from small drawings, and I assumed all three pins go into the toggle. The picture shows only one blue pin entering the tower. I recorded that pin (b85) as passing into pin-hole.1 of b71.
This is the fit that is uncertain. The other pins may also enter b71's other pin holes.
Step 17 turns the model and puts a Pearl Gold cheese slope (b89) as the pyramid tip on top of the two blue slopes.
The catalogue lists the blue slopes with only anti-studs and no top stud, so the way the tip attaches is unclear. I recorded it as resting on both b83 and b84, and the edges use no port names.
Page 26 starts the cobra, built as 3 identical body segments (3x box). Step 1 puts a Black 2x2 plate on each of three Dark Bluish Gray ball bricks (lego-57908). I listed all three copies.
The page's parts box also lists three Dark Tan jumper plates and three Pearl Gold cheese slopes per set of three. Only step 1 is shown, so I did not place them yet.
Step 2 adds a Dark Tan jumper plate (lego-87580) to each of the three segments. Step 3 adds a Pearl Gold cheese slope on the centre stud of each jumper. The whole sub-assembly is built 3 times (3x).
The cheese slopes appear orange in the picture. I took them as Pearl Gold because that is the only matching slope colour in the parts list.

Page 28 starts a body-section sub-assembly built 4 times (4x). The parts box shows totals for all four: 12 Dark Tan 2x4 plates, 8 Dark Blue wedge plates, 8 Dark Orange tiles, 8 socket bricks and 16 curved Pearl Gold bricks.

Steps 1 and 2 put two black socket bricks (lego-92013) side by side on a Dark Tan 2x4 plate, then cover them with a second Dark Tan 2x4 plate. That is 2 plates and 2 bricks per copy, so I listed all four copies. The third tan plate, the wedges, tiles and curved bricks come in later steps.
The copy ids run b102-b105, b106-b109, b110-b113 and b114-b117.
The sandwich order is read from the small drawings. The edges use no port names.

Page 29 finishes the 4x body-section sub-assembly begun on page 28. Per copy it adds 4 curved Pearl Gold bricks (the orange band), 2 Dark Blue wedge plates, a third Dark Tan 2x4 plate and 2 Dark Orange 1x2 tiles. The totals match the page 28 parts box: 16 curved bricks, 8 wedges, 12 tan plates (3 per copy), 8 tiles.

The small drawings make the exact stacking unclear. I assumed the curved bricks and wedges sit on the top tan plate (b105 for copy 1), the extra tan plate sits on the wedges, and each tile sits on a wedge. Some of these placements are guesses.
The repeat's external endpoint b105 is the top plate of copy 1. Copies 2 to 4 use b109, b113 and b117, set through attach overrides.
Edges use no port names because the stud positions are not clear.

Page 30 joins the 4 body sections and the 3 ball segments into one chain: section 1, ball segment, section 2, ball segment, section 3, ball segment, section 4. Each ball of a segment snaps into a socket of the neighbouring section's end socket brick.

Each section has two socket bricks, one at each end. Which of the two is at which end is assumed, so I used b104, b107, b108, b111, b112 and b115 for the joins. The other socket bricks (b103, b116, b105's partners) stay free for the ends of the chain.
No new pieces appear on this page.
Page 31 starts the tail (assembly 3). Steps 1 to 3 put a socket brick (b119) on one end of a 2x4 plate (b118) and a ball brick (b120) on the other end.
The plate colour looks dark olive, but the parts count (13 Dark Tan 2x4 plates, 12 used earlier) points to Dark Tan, so I used that.
The parts box also shows a Dark Blue wedge plate, two curved bricks, a cheese slope, a jumper plate and two tail pieces. They are not placed on this page, so I did not add them.

Page 32 finishes the tail. Step 4 adds a Dark Blue wedge plate (b121) and two curved gold bricks (b122, b123). Step 5 adds a Dark Tan jumper plate (b124) and the tail's middle section (b125). Step 6 adds the tail end (b126) and a gold cheese slope (b127) on the jumper.
The tail middle section (b125) is assumed to push its pin into the axle hole of the socket brick b119, on the side opposite the ball. The arrow in the picture is not exact.
The curved bricks are assumed to sit on the studs of b119 and b120, and the jumper on the wedge and both curved bricks. These placements are estimated from small pictures.
Edges use no port names where the stud positions are unclear.
Page 33 attaches the finished tail to the last body section of the cobra chain. The ball of b120 snaps into the free end socket brick of section 4 (b116).
No new pieces appear on this page.
Page 34 starts the cobra head sub-assembly. Step 1 puts a hinge plate (b129) on a dark 2x4 plate (b128). Step 2 adds a ball brick (b130) on the same plate.
The 2x4 plate colour is uncertain. It looks dark olive like the other dark plates, so I recorded Black. The parts-list counts for 2x4 plates do not fit exactly, so this could be Dark Tan instead.
The edges use no port names because the stud positions are not clear.

Step 3 adds two more black 2x2 corner plates (b131, b132) around the hinge and ball brick on the plate b128. Step 4 adds a red plate (b133) and a long dark plate (b134) on top, with the black plate over the red.

I took the red plate as Red 2x4 (lego-3020) and the long dark plate as Black 2x6 (lego-3795), since the black 2x6 has not been used elsewhere. That makes the earlier red plate b17 a possible mis-identification, because the parts list has only one Red 2x4. The step 4 picture is small.
The red plate is assumed to rest on both corner plates and b130. Edges use no port names.
Step 5 adds a Dark Blue wedge plate (b135) at the ball end of the head sub-assembly. Step 6 adds four curved Pearl Gold bricks (b136 to b139) beside and in front of the wedge.
Which curved brick sits on which piece is not clear from the small picture. I assumed two sit on b134 and two on b130. The edges use no port names.
Step 7 adds a Dark Tan 2x4 plate (b140) on top of the wedge and the four curved bricks. Step 8 turns the head over and adds two Pearl Gold round 1x1 plates (b141, b142).
The round plates are assumed to sit one on b130 and one on b133. This is estimated from the small picture. Edges use no port names.

Step 9 builds the cobra's lower jaw. A tan 1x2 plate (b144) and two red clip plates (b145, b146) go on the cobra head piece (b143), and the head is fitted to the red plate b133 of the neck. Step 10 adds a red round plate (b147) as the tongue and two white fangs (b148, b149) clipped into the red clips.
The two red clip pieces are read as Red Plate Special 1x1 with Clip Vertical (lego-4085c), the only matching red part in the list. The round tongue is the Red Boat Stud plate (lego-2654).

Which studs and anti-studs are used is not clear from the pictures. The head is assumed to be joined to b133 only. The round plate b147 is assumed to rest on the tan plate b144. Edges use no port names except the fang clips.
Page 39 attaches the finished head to the front end of the cobra body chain. The ball of b130 snaps into the free socket of section 1 (b103).
No new pieces appear on this page.

Page 40 starts a new sub-assembly (assembly 12). The parts box shows a left and right 3x2 wedge plate, a red 2x2 tile, a red clip plate, a black 2x2 plate, a hinge plate and a jumper plate. Steps 1 and 2 only join the two wedge plates (b150, b151).

Which wedge sits on which, and exactly how they overlap, is unclear from the drawing. I recorded a single joined edge between them. Step 2 may also show a hinge finger, but I did not add the hinge plate because it is not clearly shown.
The page's parts box lists several other pieces that are not placed yet. I will add them when later pages show them in place.

Page 41 continues assembly 12. The hinge plate (b152) is already visible as a knob on page 40 step 2, but I only record it now. Step 3 adds a black 2x2 plate (b153), step 4 a red 2x2 tile (b154) on it, and step 5 a red clip plate (b155) on the wedge studs.
The hinge plate is read as the Black 60471 with 2 fingers, the only hinge plate in black in the list. Its place on the wedges is assumed.
Which studs hold each piece is estimated from small pictures. Edges use no port names.
Page 42 attaches the red tongue sub-assembly (assembly 12) to the cobra head. The hinge plate b152 meshes with the hinge plate b129 on the head, in the mouth area.
No new pieces appear on this page. The hinge join is my reading of the arrow.
Step 13 adds two Dark Tan jumper plates. One (b156) goes on top of the head plate b140. The other (b157) goes on the top plate of the first body section (seg1.p).
These two plus the four earlier ones make the six Dark Tan jumper plates in the parts list.
Edges use no port names because the stud positions are not clear.
Step 14 puts the cobra hood (b158) over the two jumper plate studs, on the head (b156) and on the first body section (b157), and caps each stud with a Trans-Clear round plate (b159, b160).

The round plates are read as Trans-Clear, the last two of the six in the parts list. The hood has only a pin port in the catalogue, so the edges use no port names, and the hood is simply joined to both jumper plates.
Which round plate caps which stud is assumed from the picture.
Step 15 puts a Dark Bluish Gray inverted dish (lego-4740) over each of the two round plates on the hood, b159 and b160.
I read the pieces as dishes, not round plates, because all eight Dark Bluish Gray round plates in the list were already used on page 12.
Which dish goes on which round plate is assumed. Edges use no port names.

Page 46 attaches the cobra to the tower. The arrow points from the first ball segment (b90) to the toggle joint (b88) on the tower's Technic brick. I recorded this as one blue axle pin (b87) of the toggle joint going into b90.
The ball brick (lego-57908) has no pin hole in the catalogue, so the exact fit is uncertain. The edge uses no port name on b90.
No new pieces appear on this page.
Page 47 shows the finished cobra statue next to the vehicle, with minifigures. It has no building step, so nothing is added.
The green snakes and the minifigures are not attached to anything in a building step, so they are not recorded.
Page 50 is a LEGO Club advertisement. It has no building step, so nothing is added.
Page 51 is the LEGO Club sign-up form. It has no building step, so nothing is added.
Page 52 is a LEGO survey advertisement and the back cover. It has no building step, so nothing is added.
